newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan chemical firms weigh joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan chemical firms weigh joint venture.

text.p: Haifa Chemicals, the world's leading producer of potassium nitrate fertiliser, is negotiating with Jordan's Arab Potash Co to set up a joint $60 million venture in Jordan, a spokesman for the Israeli company said on Thursday.
"The joint venture would be for the setting up of a plant to produce raw materials for our Israeli plants," the spokesman said, adding that negotiations were in their initial stages.

Haifa Chemicals has two plants in Israel, one in Haifa and the other at Mishor Rotem in the Negev desert. The Haifa plant is shut down due to a dispute between management and the union over a wage agreement.

The spokesman said that despite the shutdown Haifa Chemicals would continue to supply customers from its Mishor Rotem plant and a plant in Vicksburg, Mississippi, owned by Trans Resources Inc, parent company of Haifa Chemicals.
